one_paragraph_summary: Against the backdrop of the TRAIN controversy, Panganiban reveals that 10 million taxpayers are owed an early Christmas bonanza: refunds or tax credits for excessive income taxes paid since 2008 under the BIR's now-voided prorating of RA 9504 exemptions. RA 9504 (signed June 17, 2008 by President Arroyo; effective July 6, 2008) raised the basic personal exemption to P50,000 regardless of civil status, increased additional per-dependent exemptions to P25,000 (max 4), and granted minimum wage earners (MWEs) full income tax exemption on their minimum wage plus statutory extras (holiday pay, overtime, night shift differential, hazard pay). The BIR's RR 10-2008 imposed a strict-construction, prorated approach: any additional compensation (commissions, allowances, honoraria) stripped MWE status and taxed the entire income. The SC unanimously voided RR 10-2008 in Soriano v. Secretary of Finance (January 24, 2017, 56 pages, per CJ Sereno): the clear legislative intent -- evidenced by Senate deliberations of Senators Escudero, Santiago, and law sponsor-petitioner Roxas -- was to grant full tax relief, overriding the strict-construction default; income taxes are annual, not semiannual; and nothing in RA 9504 suggests prorated application. Finance Secretary and BIR Commissioner were directed to grant refunds, tax credits, or withholding adjustments. Panganiban estimates the total refund at about P20 billion -- P2,000 on average per taxpayer -- and calls on Finance Secretary Dominguez and BIR Commissioner Dulay (who had no role in the voided prorating) to craft the revenue regulation in time for Christmas.
